messages:
kevin: heads up — trying to bring up `open-llm/foo-chat` for Redwood staging. HF model requires `trust_remote_code=True` and registers a custom config class. conversion script fails during auto_map resolution and tokenizer conversion. stack trace below.

sophia: ohhh the `trust_remote_code` bit again. what's the exact error?

kevin: paste of the error: `TypeError: FooConfig.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'hidden_size'` when running `redwood-convert-hf --model open-llm/foo-chat --out /tmp/foo-convert`. Also tokenizer warnings: `Added tokens found in special_tokens_map not in tokenizer vocab: ['<|user|>', '<|assistant|>']`.

alex: two things we see often: 1) custom config requires args not present in HF config.json unless `from_pretrained` path triggers custom class, 2) auto_map in transformers points to class path like `foo_arch.FooForCausalLM` which isn't importable unless trust_remote_code is allowed. Did you set `--trust-remote-code` flag on the converter?

kevin: yep tried `--trust-remote-code`, converter logs show `AutoConfig` picked up `FooConfig` via auto_map, but later our internal model loader tries to instantiate with `FooConfig(**hf_config)` and crashes because HF authors expect `hidden_size` computed by a different factory method.

maria: can you paste `config.json` from the repo? sometimes authors store computed fields under `model_args` or a nested dict.

kevin: snippet from config.json: ```json
{"architectures": ["FooForCausalLM"], "auto_map": {"AutoModelForCausalLM": "foo_arch.FooForCausalLM"}, "n_heads": 16, "d_model": 1024}```

sophia: aha — they use nonstandard keys (`d_model`/`n_heads`) rather than `hidden_size`. Our converter expects canonical names. Two options: map keys during conversion (`d_model` -> `hidden_size`) or load with the custom class (trust_remote_code) and then serialize a canonical config.

alex: mapping is fragile but quick for staging. Add a transform step in `redwood-convert-hf` that looks for common aliases: `d_model` -> `hidden_size`, `n_heads` -> `num_attention_heads`. Also handle `vocab_special_tokens` -> `special_tokens_map`.

kevin: tried a local patch that maps `d_model`->`hidden_size`, `n_heads`->`num_attention_heads`. Conversion proceeds further but tokenizer mapping still fails: special tokens are present in `tokenizer.json` as added_tokens with ids > vocab_size causing our `merge_tokens` step to error: `IndexError: token id 50256 out of range`.

maria: special tokens often use fast tokenizer artifacts. Try exporting the tokenizer with `tokenizer.save_pretrained(out_dir, legacy_format=True)` or load the tokenizer with `use_fast=False` before conversion — that flattens the added tokens into vocab. Also check for `added_tokens.json`.

kevin: good tip. switching to `use_fast=False` avoids the token id error but we now hit model runtime mismatch in quantized path: `RuntimeError: KV cache shape mismatch` when running with 8-bit quantization in CI. Could be the custom attention implementation from the remote code.

sophia: this is expected: trust_remote_code models sometimes replace attention modules with custom CUDA kernels that don't support our standard quantization wrappers. For quant experiments, either 1) run quant tests without `trust_remote_code` and fall back to a compatible HF-equivalent architecture, or 2) ask model authors to provide `quantize` hooks, or 3) run quantization at a different granularity (per-layer float->int8 emulation) in a testbed.

kevin: we need a short-term workaround to unblock the staging evals. Any preferences?

alex: short term: strip custom modules after loading with `trust_remote_code`, then convert to our standard module classes if we can map names 1:1. Risky but works for preliminary quality regressions. We should gate that behind a feature flag.

maria: long term: push a PR to `open-llm/foo-chat` suggesting a canonical config keys section and a `to_standard_config()` method. Also ask them to register tokenizer special tokens in `special_tokens_map` (HF convention) so conversion is deterministic.

kevin: will try the strip-and-replace approach. sharing quick repro command for infra: `python -c "from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer; m=AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('open-llm/foo-chat', trust_remote_code=True); m.save_pretrained('/tmp/foo'); t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('open-llm/foo-chat', use_fast=False); t.save_pretrained('/tmp/foo')"`

infra-bot: deploy-check: conversion VM image has `transformers==4.33.1` and `accelerate==0.20`. If you need newer features of `trust_remote_code`, request image bump.

alex: one more diagnostic trick: `python -c "from transformers import AutoConfig; c=AutoConfig.from_pretrained('open-llm/foo-chat', trust_remote_code=True); print(c.to_dict())"` to inspect which keys the custom config expects.

kevin: thanks. i'll iterate and post back a minimal patch to the converter. plan: 1) run with `use_fast=False` tokenizer export, 2) map common config aliases, 3) add a feature-flagged module-rewrite step for custom classes to our conversion flow, 4) re-run quant tests in CI with `--quant-mode=emulate` first.

sophia: sounds good. please tag me when you push the patch. also add a tiny eval set to capture chat-turn formatting regressions (user/assistant special tokens) — we've bitten by that before. :eyes:

kevin: will do. thanks all.
